mutations.because: A NUMBER MOVED — the fault M3 is most likely to commit while unifying five rules into one table. An absent `minDistance` would resolve to 2 instead of 1, so every brief that never wrote the key gets a different, stricter draw. The goldens file catches it as a changed `policyHash`, which is the strongest available form of 'the brief plans identically': the hash is recorded pre-change against the merge-base sources and carries all five integers, so no reader can update it alongside the code and call it still-passing.

The same number-moved fault on the field whose default is the easiest to get wrong, because 0 reads as 'nothing'. A per-product floor of 1 where there was none changes which creatives the draw is even allowed to produce. Caught by the pre-change hash, not by an arithmetic assertion — a `perProduct` of 1 is perfectly plausible and every count/ratio assertion in the suite stays green under it.

The fifth row on its own, and the reason the per-field tests are not one loop: `perProduct` and `perRatio` are the two rows that genuinely DO agree, so a reader is tempted to assert them together. Moved alone, `perRatio`'s default is a floor on every ratio of every brief that never asked for one. Its own named test is what sees it.

**SL-D6, reverted through the table.** The floor of 1 is now a row rather than a literal in `fromBrief`, so the row has to be load-bearing or the stamp has moved without anyone editing the code that enforced it. Dropping it to 0 lets an explicit `minDistance: 0` reach the planner again — the hole SG-D7 measured at 83 of 120 distinct. The existing SL-D6 tests, written before this lane and untouched by it, are what go red: the policy's own refusal and the ceiling case that depends on it.

The substitution has to land on a value the planner REFUSES — otherwise a blank or unparseable count becomes a silently plannable brief, and the preview estimates a campaign the operator never described. One below the floor is that value by construction; `count.min` is one step away and is plannable.
